correctness.rationale: The balanced mode transformation multiplies the two input factors to give (c†²−d†²)^n. Distinct output occupations are orthogonal on each side; including their factorial normalizations gives p_{n,k}=a_k a_{n-k}, whose sum is one by convolution. On k<=n/2 the scaled bulk endpoint mass is bounded by C n^{q/2−1} times the sum of (k+1)^(-q/2) through δn, so uniform interior Stirling and then δ→0 give the beta integral for 0<q<2. At q=2 replacing a_{n-k}² by 1/(πn) on either half produces total error O(1/n), since (k+1)a_k² is bounded; the harmonic sums give the coefficient 2/π². For q>2 the two reflected half-sums each converge by a summable majorant C a_k^q, with no midpoint contribution. The integrable endpoint bound for f_n log f_n establishes the von Neumann constant without interchanging the n limit and a q derivative; the expectation of log x under the arcsine density is −2 log 2. The partial transpose trace norm equals F_n(1/2)²; the beta evaluation gives the stated gamma constant and subtracting 1 does not change the limiting slope. The increasing successive ratios of a_k put the largest weight at either edge. The frozen script and its stated observations were inspected, not executed; the limit verification is analytic.
residual_risks: All orders in the limit are fixed; no uniform near-critical scaling or imperfect beam splitter is certified.

value.rationale: The formula gives sharp weights of three different asymptotic mechanisms in a standard optical entanglement source. It quantifies when the continuum arcsine law is usable and when the lattice edges must be kept, and separates the leading von Neumann and min-entropy coefficients. The useful result is this fixed-order classification and its constants, not a rediscovery of the photon-count probabilities or the q=2 calculation alone.
residual_risks: No claim about a finite-size scaling window centered at q=2 or robustness under nonideal optics.
